summary: Former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper leads former RNC chair Michael Whatley 54 to 40 in an Oct. 7 to 11 WSOC and WRAL SurveyUSA poll, and GOP groups including the Senate Leadership Fund have paused ads while Whatley's campaign went dark on TV for a stretch, per WSOC and the Daily Wire. The race is about costs, tariffs and health care on Cooper's side and crime, taxes and Cooper's record as governor on Whatley's, per ABC11 and Spectrum News.

issues.why: Cooper says Congress should reclaim power over tariffs that hurt consumers, while Whatley promises lower taxes and higher take home pay.
Whatley attacks a 2021 COVID era settlement that led to early prison releases, and Cooper cites his record prosecuting criminals as attorney general.
Cooper says the One Big Beautiful Bill Act Whatley backed cut ACA subsidies, while Whatley blames Cooper for rising premiums and rural closures.
Whatley served as Trump's recovery czar for western North Carolina, and Cooper's campaign calls his tenure a failure while Whatley's side cites billions in federal aid.
Cooper opposes Duke Energy rate hikes and says Whatley lobbied for utilities, while Whatley backs gas and nuclear and faults Cooper for the Atlantic Coast Pipeline.

storylines.title: Whatley campaign goes dark on TV
storylines.what: Whatley's last broadcast ad aired Oct. 7 and his campaign had no future TV reservations, though it called the pause temporary, while Cooper's side held about a four to one booking edge.

storylines.title: Poll shows Cooper up 14
storylines.what: A WSOC and WRAL SurveyUSA poll had Cooper at 54 percent and Whatley at 40, though a local analyst said he expects the final margin to be closer.

storylines.title: Whatley calls poll trash
storylines.what: Whatley dismissed a poll showing Cooper up 15, said other surveys show a tight race, and said he has visited all 100 counties.

storylines.title: MAGA Inc offshoot spends 8 million attacking Cooper
storylines.what: The No Going Back PAC, tied to Trump's super PAC, spent close to 8 million dollars in early September mostly on TV ads attacking Cooper.

storylines.title: Health care clash
storylines.what: Whatley said premiums rose and rural facilities closed under Cooper, and Cooper said Whatley backed a bill that stripped ACA subsidies from North Carolinians.

storylines.title: No debate agreed
storylines.what: Spectrum News, the state broadcasters association and WUNC invited both candidates to debate, but neither had accepted.

storylines.title: Dueling stops on crime and costs
storylines.what: Whatley, flanked by law enforcement, hit Cooper over COVID era prison releases, while Cooper said Trump has not delivered on costs and touted his prosecutor record.

events.title: Prison release attack
events.prompt: Ads say thousands of inmates were released early under a COVID era settlement while Cooper was governor. How does your campaign handle crime?

opts.label: Reform and prevention
opts.say: Defend criminal justice reform and invest in prevention and reentry programs.

opts.label: Cite the prosecutor record
opts.say: Point to years prosecuting violent criminals and passing tougher bail and gang laws.

opts.label: Back the blue hard
opts.say: Stand with sheriffs and say we need to enforce the law, not reimagine it.

events.title: Tariffs and prices
events.prompt: Voters say prices for housing, health care and essentials are squeezing them, and tariffs are a live issue. What is your cost of living message?

opts.label: Rein in tariffs
opts.say: Say Congress should take back tariff power and block utility rate hikes.

opts.label: Make stuff cost less
opts.say: Run a pocketbook tour on child care, housing and drug prices without attacking anyone.

opts.label: Cut taxes and rates
opts.say: Promise lower taxes, lower interest rates and more jobs under Trump's agenda.

events.title: Health insurance subsidies
events.prompt: Many families lost ACA subsidies after the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, and premiums are a top complaint. Where do you stand?

opts.label: Restore subsidies
opts.say: Vow to restore ACA subsidies and protect Medicaid expansion.

opts.label: Fix rural care
opts.say: Focus on keeping rural hospitals open with bipartisan funding.

opts.label: Credit Trump on drugs
opts.say: Credit Trump for lower drug prices and blame Cooper for premium hikes as governor.

events.title: Money gap late in race
events.prompt: Outside groups on your side have paused TV ads with polls showing a double digit gap. How do you spend the final weeks?

opts.label: Flood the airwaves
opts.say: Book heavy TV and digital to close the deal with a broad message.

opts.label: Ground game
opts.say: Pull ads and invest in visiting all 100 counties and turnout.

opts.label: Bring in Trump
opts.say: Hold rallies with Trump and Vance to energize the base.

ads.theme: Close to 8 million dollars in TV ads attacking Cooper.
About 18.6 million dollars in booked TV time for the closing weeks.
Whatley says a closing message ad is coming after a temporary pause.

regions.name: Research Triangle
regions.note: Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill form the fastest growing Democratic stronghold, with Johnston as a Republican exurb.

regions.name: Charlotte metro
regions.note: Deep blue Mecklenburg surrounded by Republican suburban and exurban counties.

regions.name: Piedmont Triad
regions.note: Greensboro and Winston Salem lean Democratic while surrounding counties are solidly Republican.

regions.name: Western North Carolina
regions.note: Mountain region still recovering from Hurricane Helene, Republican overall with a Democratic hub in Asheville.

regions.name: Northeast and Black Belt
regions.note: Rural counties with large Black populations that anchor Democratic votes in the east.

regions.name: Southeast and coast
regions.note: Military towns, beach retirees and Robeson's swing Lumbee vote, leaning Republican outside Wilmington and Fayetteville.
